messages.subject: [R-sig-Debian] APT key for cloud.r-project.org expired
messages.body_plain:
Dear CRAN Debian backport users,

yes, this is an issue for Debian bookworm. One way to solve it right away is 
to use/upgrade to trixie, which considers the signatures still valid, as the 
key was not expired when the repositories were signed.

I am currently travelling, but plan to generate a new key on Thursday morning 
(not sure how much time it will take, the last time I did was five years 
ago...) and sign the repos with the updated key in order to satisfy apt from 
bookworm.

Another way would be add trusted = yes to the corresponding entry in your apt 
source.list, but I think this completely skips signature verification so in 
case one of my systems gets compromised, you may get malware. In case you 
decide to do this anyways, make sure to revert it after I have published the 
new key.

Cheers,

Johannes

messages.body_plain:
Dear users of the R backports for Debian on CRAN,

as of today (as a matter of fact since half an hour), the repository index 
files for the Debian backports on CRAN are signed with my new key
with fingerprint BA4EE5DE858FFFA7CFD8563908FC7B745769E9E4.

You can fetch it with

gpg --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com \
    --recv-key 'BA4EE5DE858FFFA7CFD8563908FC7B745769E9E4'

and, if you followed configuration hints for Debian on CRAN, put it to the 
correct location

gpg --armor --export 'BA4EE5DE858FFFA7CFD8563908FC7B745769E9E4' | \
    sudo tee /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/cran_debian_key.asc

Kind regards,

Johannes

messages.subject_clean: Corrected instructions for R backports for Debian
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Pierre-Andre Cornillon noticed that instructions for secure apt in the Debian 
page on CRAN [1] were actually unnecessarily insecure. Instead of placing the 
key used for veryfing the repository signatures into
/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/ they should be put into /etc/apt/keyrings/ which is 
already present in Debian systems since bookworm.

I have updated the instructions accordingly. In case you have already used the
instructions published yesterday for downloading my new key, please move it
from /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/cran_debian_key.asc to 
/etc/keyrings/cran_debian.asc and adapt your source entries accordingly.

Cheers,

Johannes

[1] https://cran.r-project.org/bin/linux/debian/

messages.subject: [R-sig-Debian] Update of JAGS to version 5.0.2
messages.body_plain:
Dear all

As you may have already seen, the rjags package has been updated to version 5-5 on CRAN:  this has a system dependency on JAGS 5.x.y, and will fail to build against the JAGS 4.x.y installation present on existing build systems (e.g. resolute-cran40 and noble-cran40).  I opened an issue with the r-universe team to let them know (https://github.com/r-universe-org/help/issues/756#issuecomment-7064164170) and was advised to post on this list to ask if the maintainers of the Debian and Ubuntu ports of JAGS can backport the latest release at https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/jags ?

I don?t have a lot of experience with Debian/Ubuntu but I have had a small role in contributing to rjags and JAGS (primarily building the macOS binaries of JAGS), and I am very willing to try and help if there are any questions/issues.

Best wishes,

Matt



Matthew Denwood BVMS PhD FHEA MRCVS
Professor of Computational and Statistical Disease Modelling
Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
University of Copenhagen

| Dear all
| 
| As you may have already seen, the rjags package has been updated to version 5-5 on CRAN:  this has a system dependency on JAGS 5.x.y, and will fail to build against the JAGS 4.x.y installation present on existing build systems (e.g. resolute-cran40 and noble-cran40).  I opened an issue with the r-universe team to let them know (https://github.com/r-universe-org/help/issues/756#issuecomment-7064164170) and was advised to post on this list to ask if the maintainers of the Debian and Ubuntu ports of JAGS can backport the latest release at https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/jags ?
| 
| I don?t have a lot of experience with Debian/Ubuntu but I have had a small role in contributing to rjags and JAGS (primarily building the macOS binaries of JAGS), and I am very willing to try and help if there are any questions/issues.

Matt raised this as he noted in a github issue for r-universe as builds on
Ubuntu-based systems now fail as jags (the binary package) is fixed at
version 4.3.2 (say in Debian stable, similar for the Ubuntu builds).

It might be worthwhile spelling out that things "are actually as they are
supposed to be".  New of packages versions got into 'Debian unstable', and
jags 5.0.2 is there. Over time these get into Debian stable and Ubuntu
release. And we commonly use these Debian 'stable' or Ubuntu 'long-term
stable' aka LTS releases ... because we want them to be stable. In other
words immutable. So by default, no changes and no new jags.

On the other hand, we are here for R and we want current R versions. So
'backports' of current R are available at CRAN in the bin/linux/debian and
bin/linux/ubuntu directories thanks to the efforts of Johannes and Michael.

Now jags has a new upgrade, and the dependencies slowly work their way
through CRAN. rjags just updated at CRAN and now need jags 5.0.*.

So Michael and Johannes:  Could you please look into proving jags 5.0.2 as
backports?  The Debian sources should be fine.

Cheers, Dirk

--

messages.body_plain:
Thanks, Michael. Before the Jammy build goes out: the Debian orig tarball
for jags 5.0.2 is the upstream 5.0.1 tarball, so the 5.0.2 backports for
Resolute and Noble are 5.0.1 code, and a Jammy build from the same sources
would be too.

How I found it, on Ubuntu 26.04 with your backport:

1. After apt upgraded jags to 5.0.2-1.2604.2 from resolute-cran40, running
jags printed "Welcome to JAGS 5.0.1", and pkg-config --modversion jags also
reports 5.0.1.

2. There is no other JAGS on the machine: type -a jags finds only
/usr/bin/jags, and ldconfig -p finds only the packaged
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libjags.so.5.

3. The package changelog shows Dirk's Debian upload (5.0.2-1, "New upstream
release", 19 Nov) and your Ubuntu rebuild (5.0.2-1.2604.2, 21 Nov,
build-dependency changes only), so neither step should have changed the
version.

4. Comparing the tarballs:

  JAGS-5.0.2.tar.gz (SourceForge)
    AC_INIT([JAGS],[5.0.2],...)
    sha256 80143e23fc6feca01d4cce440fd8f6aa865a03333ed36baf9e0ce30a8f9e3aea

  jags_5.0.2.orig.tar.gz (deb.debian.org pool)
    AC_INIT([JAGS],[5.0.1],...)
    sha256 0888571b1812c8ce076ad6326c66f96a0ae7762497c346cd7eb32d35a62105d4

  JAGS-5.0.1.tar.gz (SourceForge)
    sha256 0888571b1812c8ce076ad6326c66f96a0ae7762497c346cd7eb32d35a62105d4

The Debian orig tarball is byte-identical to upstream 5.0.1. So jags
5.0.2-1 in unstable, and the backports built from it, are JAGS 5.0.1 under
a 5.0.2 version number. Dirk, the fix is presumably a 5.0.2-2 upload with
the correct orig tarball.

Best,
Dale

On 22 November 2026 at 12:06, Dale Steele wrote:
| Nice! One more for the JAGS 5 transition: r2u's r-cran-runjags
| 2.3.0-5-1.ca2604.1 (Resolute) links libjags.so.4 (per ldd on
| runjags/libs/runjags.so), but its Depends is an unversioned "jags". apt
| will happily upgrade jags to 5.x underneath it, leaving runjags' module
| unloadable. It probably needs a rebuild against 5.0.2.1, and ideally a
| versioned dependency. Noble and Jammy builds are likely the same. Best.

Packages such as 'jags' that bring their own shared library are easy to
package as just one package, but would likely be better packaged as set with
'jags' (the frontend), 'libjags$SONAME' (the runtime) and 'libjags-dev'. That
would allow two libjags$SONAME to coexist. We haven't needed it yet so I
haven't done, and I may not have the bandwidth to redo this (properly).  So
it is what it is, at least for now.

As r2u is using Ubuntu, it too was held back by the lack of a jags5 package
for the different LTS branches. We have two+two now, jammy is pending (and we
could skip that as we do for other 'newer' and demanding packages) but noble
and resolute should and can get rebuilds (and are in fact just done). Just
how 'rjags' was (re-)done this morning, I just turned 'runjags' on now as
well.  In general, when you observe something like this for
'r2u' it might be most efficient to file an issue at the r2u repo (which may
have more visibility / easier search than this list).

A few lines from a quick check in a 26.04 container just now:

  [...]
  Setting up libltdl7:amd64 (2.5.4-9) ...
  Setting up r-cran-coda (0.19-4.1-1.ca2604.1) ...
  Setting up jags (5.0.2-1.2604.2) ...
  Setting up r-cran-rjags (5-5-1.ca2604.1) ...
  Setting up r-cran-runjags (2.3.0-5-1.ca2604.2) ...
  Processing triggers for libc-bin (2.43-2ubuntu2.4) ...
  [...]
  
and
  root at 401970cb67f0:/work# ldd /usr/lib/R/site-library/runjags/libs/runjags.so | grep jags
          libjags.so.5 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libjags.so.5 (0x00007a4480d77000)
  root at 401970cb67f0:/work# 

Thanks also for this reminder!

Dirk
